Chapter Eight: Sustaining Passion—Weathering the Highs and Lows
You know, those first days of following your “Must”—that thing you feel called to do—they’re usually packed with excitement. There’s this electric sense of discovery, a real rush, almost like you’re finally on the path you were meant for.
But as weeks turn into months, that initial spark can start to fade. The work settles into a routine, obstacles begin to pop up, and sometimes, doubts creep right back in.
And here’s the honest truth—keeping your passion alive becomes its own kind of challenge.
Think about someone who decided to write every morning. At first, it felt magical—words just poured out. But after a few months, that magic got harder to find. Suddenly, the blank page looked intimidating.
It seemed much easier to sleep in, check emails, or do pretty much anything except sit down and write.
The thrill of starting had turned into the grind of simply keeping at it.
Most of us expect passion to be effortless—like motivation on tap, always ready to go. But the reality? It’s messier than that.
There are days when everything feels tedious, when progress is slow, and those sparks of inspiration are nowhere in sight.
So, what separates the people who keep going from those who give up? It’s not talent. It’s not luck. It’s commitment.
One artist compared the creative journey to a series of seasons. There are times of growth and abundance—when ideas just flow and everything feels possible.
But then, there are winters—periods full of doubt, frustration, and creative drought.
The real trick is to keep showing up, even when it’s hard. To trust that, just like the seasons, things will shift again.
It’s about honoring the process, even when the results aren’t clear.
Keeping your passion alive calls for patience and resilience. You have to be willing to embrace the whole experience—the good and the tough parts.
It’s about finding joy in the work itself, not just in whatever outcome you’re hoping for.
It means celebrating the small wins, learning from the setbacks, and always staying connected to your deeper “why.”
Here’s something lots of people miss—passion isn’t just something you have or don’t have. It’s a practice.
It’s built, nurtured, and sustained over time.
The journey? It’s rarely easy. But honestly, it’s always worth it.
